headline: High: AutoGen can write/execute code while Pipecat can relay rich shared-bus content to third-party services, creating default risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen ingests and executes tool/code outputs in multi-agent chats, while Pipecat runs on a shared bus and handles text/audio/video content. If Pipecat forwards attacker-controlled content into AutoGen’s workspace or stdin/stdout, instructions can be smuggled across the pair. The pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards untrusted text into AutoGen prompts or stdin/stdout
IF both agents share a bus or workspace without provenance tagging
mitigations: Add a strict content firewall between Pipecat outputs and AutoGen prompts
Prefix all cross-agent messages with immutable provenance labels
Disable automatic execution of any text received from Pipecat
Route only allowlisted message types across the bridge
requires-engineering: add schema validation and prompt-injection filtering

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen can read/write local files and use broad network egress, while Pipecat touches text, audio, video, and conversation state and can call many external model APIs. In a shared workspace or bus, sensitive application data can flow from one agent into the other and then out to third parties. The blast radius includes exfiltration, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF the two agents share a workspace, bus, or mounted files
IF Pipecat sends conversation state or media to external STT/LLM/TTS services
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials for each agent
Block sensitive files from the AutoGen working directory
Disable external API calls for Pipecat on sensitive runs
Use redaction before any cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: enforce per-data-class egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has filesystem write and shell execution, while Pipecat supports shared-bus concurrency and multiple instances. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared files or state if co-located, creating race conditions and lost updates. The conflict is plausible in default deployments but not proven to be unrestricted, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or state store
IF Pipecat instances share a bus while AutoGen writes artifacts into that bus-backed workspace
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories and state stores
Serialize writes with a lock file or queue
Disable AutoGen writes except to a scratch path
Run one agent per process with separate service accounts
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, facts, and tool outputs, and Pipecat can consume text in real time and route it onward through LLM/STT/TTS services. If Pipecat treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or user-facing speech without verification. Because the pair can act on each other’s outputs by default, high is appropriate.
conditions: IF Pipecat forwards AutoGen output to a downstream model or action step without verification
IF AutoGen-generated facts are spoken or acted on by Pipecat
mitigations: Insert a human or rule-based verification step before Pipecat acts
Require citations or structured schemas from AutoGen outputs
Reject free-form commands from AutoGen unless explicitly allowlisted
Log and review all cross-agent handoffs
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data, while Pipecat touches audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics and can send data to many external services. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so a concrete breach cannot be proven; however, the default multi-service flow creates a plausible retention and jurisdiction mismatch risk, warranting medium under uncertainty.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through Pipecat services outside the required jurisdiction
IF retention or logging settings differ across the two agents for the same data class
mitigations: Classify data before any handoff
Disable analytics/metrics for regulated runs
Use region-locked providers only
Document retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for residency and retention
